title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-incident-breadcrumbs
content:
Context / quick summary:
- On 2026-02-26 we started seeing a ~20-30% drop in sustained throughput for the text-generation route (gptx-13b-quant) on Dedicated pool A compared to baseline from last week. Latency p50 unchanged, p95 up ~5-10ms.
- Initial suspicion: continuous batching config change or recent KV-cache refactor interacting with batching/windowing.
- This doc is my working breadcrumbs: commands tried, error snippets, measurements, hypotheses, and next actions.

Observed symptoms / metrics (notes):
- During steady-state traffic (avg QPS 420 reqs/s):
  - Baseline (2026-02-20): 22k tokens/s aggregate across pool A (8 GPUs).
  - Current (2026-02-26): 15.5k tokens/s aggregate. ~29% regression.
  - GPU util (nvidia-smi): similar % utilization but more memory copies per second reported in perf counters.
  - CPU-side: more frequent micro bursts of higher load when batching windows flush.
- Logs show repeated messages: "batch window closed early: min-delay exceeded" around same timeframe as throughput drop.
- KV-cache hit rate slightly lower (drop from 0.87 -> 0.82) after deploy on 2026-02-25 (PR 2145).

Commands / queries I ran (timestamped):
- Reproducing locally with dev harness (single-GPU):
  - ./dev/harness --model gptx-13b-quant --concurrency 16 --qps 100 --seq-len 512 --batching continuous --run-10m > harness.log 2>&1
  - observed average tokens/s lower than expected; harness.log shows many "flush-window" events.

- On the dedicated pool node (ssh into gpu-03):
  - sudo journalctl -u redwood-serving -f --since "2026-02-26 08:00" | grep -E "batch|kv-cache|flush" > /tmp/serve-debug.log
  - docker exec -it runtime /bin/bash -c "./perf/measure_throughput.sh gptx-13b-quant"
  - nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o TD > /tmp/gpu-mon.txt (30s sample)

Relevant log snippets (redacted):
- serve-debug.log:
  [2026-02-26T09:12:03.812Z] INFO runtime.batch: batch window closed early: min-delay exceeded (configured_min_ms=3, observed=4.8)
  [2026-02-26T09:12:03.824Z] DEBUG runtime.batcher: flush triggered: active_slots=12 queued=48 avg_wait_ms=5.1
  [2026-02-26T09:12:03.825Z] WARN runtime.kvcache: evicting stale entries due to mem pressure (pool=pool-A gpu=3)
  [2026-02-26T09:12:03.830Z] DEBUG runtime.kernel: selected kernel variant: fast-attn-v2 seq=512 batch=12

- perf tool snippet:
  tokens_generated: 15432/s
  max_batch_seen: 16
  avg_batch_size: 8.4
  batch_wait_ms_p50: 3.6
  batch_wait_ms_p95: 9.2
  memcpy_count: 3.1k/s

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Continuous-batching window tuning regression: new default min-delay/min-batch thresholds are too low, causing many early flushes and smaller average batch sizes, hurting tokens/s.
2) KV-cache refactor (PR 2145) introduced additional memcpy/lock contention on cache lookups which increases CPU scheduling jitter and prevents batches accumulating. (support: increased memcpy_count and cache hit drop)
3) Kernel scheduling/variant selection changed for specific seq/batch combos causing less efficient kernels to be used more often. (logs show fast-attn-v2 selected but maybe less optimal for current layout)
4) Workload distribution change (slower tail callers) increasing variance and causing more frequent flushes.

Quick experiments & results:
- Reverse PR 2145 on a staging node (reverted to previous kv-cache):
  - tokens/s recovered ~+8% (not full recovery). Suggests PR contributed but not sole cause.
- Bumping batching min-delay from 3ms -> 6ms in runtime config for pool-A (hotfix):
  - avg_batch_size increased 8.4 -> 11.2, tokens/s +18% (partial recovery). p95 latency increased 7ms -> 12ms but still within SLA for Dedicated.
- Forcing kernel variant selection to fast-attn-v1 via env var on staging:
  - mixed results; tokens/s similar to baseline in some runs but unstable across runs.

What doesn't seem to be the main issue:
- GPU memory capacity: no OOMs seen, memory utilization stable.
- Network: no obvious network drops, RTTs unchanged.

Short-term mitigation applied (2026-02-28):
- Increased min-delay to 6ms for pool-A continuous-batching config (canary 10% nodes -> 100%).
- Rolled back KV-cache opt in non-critical shard (partial rollback).
- Added extra metrics: per-batch memcpy_count, kvcache-lock-wait-ms, batch-flush-reason histogram.

Open questions / next actions:
- We need to instrument more precise lock contention metrics inside KV-cache (how often do we block on mutex vs try-lock fail?).
- Re-run controlled A/B with: (A) new min-delay 6ms + reverted KV-cache PR, (B) old min-delay 3ms + reverted KV-cache PR, (C) new min-delay + PR 2145. Measure tokens/s, avg batch size, memcpy_count, kv hit rate.
- Investigate whether kernel selector is mis-ranking variants after recent codegen changes (compare kernel microbenchmarks across variant inputs).
- Consider increasing backoff window adaptively rather than static min-delay; maybe base on current QPS or observed avg_wait_ms.

Commands to run for A/B (copy for later):
- ./tools/run_ab_test --pool pool-A --configA batching.min_delay_ms=6 kvcache.revert=true --configB batching.min_delay_ms=3 kvcache.revert=true --duration 2h --metrics tokens_s,avg_batch_size,memcpy_count,kv_hit_rate --tag INF-4823-abtest

Notes to self:
- Talk to Marcus about the KV-cache implementation details and lock profiles he added. He mentioned an experimental memcpy optimization that touches a temp buffer; could be the extra memory copies we're seeing.
- Ping infra SRE about whether any kube kubelet kubelet-level scheduling changes happened around 2026-02-25.
- Add a small synthetic load generator that produces steady seq-len distribution matching production to run microbenchmarks on kernel variants.

References / links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2145 (kv-cache refactor)
- JIRA: INF-4823 (incident ticket)
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime thread ts:1677823456

Immediate next steps (today):
- Kick off the A/B test (Marcus + me).
- Add lock-wait instrumentation to kv-cache (Sofia will help on the change).
- Summarize findings in INF-4823 ticket and update on Slack.

If I don't get back to this doc: steps to reproduce quickly:
1) Use dev harness with --concurrency 32 --qps 420 --seq-len 512 --batching continuous.
2) Toggle batching.min_delay_ms between 3 and 6 and observe avg_batch_size and tokens/s.
3) Revert PR 2145 and compare results.

-- Aisha
